channel.title: The Epoch Institute — Research Series
channel.description: Thematic essays on civilisational rise and collapse.

item.title: Series 05 — The Military Revolution
item.description: Technology, Tactics, and the Shifting Balance of Power. How advances in military technology — the stirrup, gunpowder, the warship — reshaped the competitive landscape between polities and enabled otherwise peripheral states to become world powers.

item.title: Series 04 — Cross-Cultural Exchange
item.description: How Empires Spread — and Were Changed by — Ideas and Culture. From Hellenisation to the Islamic Golden Age to the Columbian Exchange, this series explores the two-way nature of cultural contact under imperial conditions and its lasting consequences.

item.title: Series 03 — The Collapse Problem
item.description: Common Patterns in Imperial Decline Across Five Millennia. Why do empires fall? Comparing the trajectories of the Western Roman Empire, the Abbasid Caliphate, the Mongol Empire, and others to identify recurring structural vulnerabilities.

item.title: Series 02 — Trade and Territory
item.description: Economic Networks Across the Ancient and Medieval World. A study of how control over trade routes, currency systems, and agricultural surplus shaped imperial ambition — and how economic disruption so often proved fatal to imperial order.

item.title: Series 01 — The Architecture of Power
item.description: How Empires Build the Structures That Sustain Them. An examination of the administrative, legal, and infrastructural systems that allowed large-scale polities to persist — and why their absence almost always preceded collapse.
